title: Frobenius equivariance of the specified common-stage pullback compositor
statement: Fix a finite field datum D with base k_0 and algebraic closure k, a prime l different from its characteristic, and an algebraic closure Ω of Q_l, as in [def-weil-finite-field-fiber; def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Let X,Y,Z be finite-type k_0-schemes, and f:X→Y, g:Y→Z morphisms over k_0. Use the specified common-stage geometric inverse images P_f, the normalized composition comparison c(f,g):P_(fg)≅P_g⋙P_f of [def-weil-derived-direct-image], and the geometric-Frobenius pullbacks Φ_X,Φ_Y,Φ_Z and normalized Frobenius squares s_f:P_f⋙Φ_X≅Φ_Y⋙P_f of [def-zl-weil-ind-sheaf-category]. Then the actual normalized compositor is equivariant: whiskerRight(c(f,g).hom,Φ_X) followed by compCommIso(s_g,s_f).hom equals s_(fg).hom followed by whiskerLeft(Φ_Z,c(f,g).hom). Here compCommIso is the pasted square with component s_f(P_g K) followed by P_f(s_g K). The equality is of natural transformations on the recorded common-stage constructible categories; it includes empty and nonreduced schemes and imposes no condition that an integral lattice be Frobenius-stable.

proof.text: The common-stage pullback representative formula and naturality of its normalized scalar comparison imply that pulling an arrow included from a fixed rational coefficient stage equals the inclusion of its rational pullback, up to the stated object equalities. The rational pure-tensor formula at scalar 1 specializes this to included integral arrows. Use HEq only to suppress equality-transport factors.

proof.text: The normalization equation of zlPullComp_existsUnique identifies its component on every included integral object with inclusion of the specified integral compositor. Replace all three compositors and the mapped compositor in the associativity equation using this formula and the preceding map formula. Apply inclusion and localization to the associativity clause of integralPullbackComposition. All omitted equality comparisons are restored by eqToHom. Every common-stage object is literally a pair of a finite field and a raw rationalized integral object, so this proves associativity at every object.

proof.text: Expand each Frobenius square as inverse compositor, geometric Frobenius naturality equality, and compositor. Precompose by the invertible c(Φ_X,fg). Apply associativity for (Φ_X,f,g), (f,Φ_Y,g), (f,g,Φ_Z), move equality comparisons by their naturality and cancel inverse compositors. The remaining equality comparisons coincide by proof irrelevance. Finally transport along functoriality of geometric base change, exactly the map_comp equality appearing in sfModelPullComposition.

lean.statement:
theorem zlWeilPullCompositorEquivariance
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (Ω : Type v) [Field Ω] [Algebra (Padic l) Ω] [IsAlgClosure (Padic l) Ω]
    {X Y Z : Over (Spec (.of D.k₀))}
    [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType Y.hom] [QuasiCompact Y.hom]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType Z.hom] [QuasiCompact Z.hom]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    Functor.whiskerRight (sfModelPullComposition D l hl Ω f g).hom
        (sfCommonStageWeilFrobeniusPullback D l hl X Ω) ≫
      (CategoryTheory.Endofunctor.IsoAlgebra.compCommIso
        (zlFrobeniusSquare D l hl Ω g) (zlFrobeniusSquare D l hl Ω f)).hom =
    (zlFrobeniusSquare D l hl Ω (f ≫ g)).hom ≫
      Functor.whiskerLeft (sfCommonStageWeilFrobeniusPullback D l hl Z Ω)
        (sfModelPullComposition D l hl Ω f g).hom
